mainTopic: Aggadic lessons on gratitude and תורה, then why idolaters' holidays require three days of preparation
overview: The amud opens by finishing a thought from the previous daf: ישראל were כפויי טובה, and משה proved it from their complaint about the מן and from אדם הראשון blaming 'the woman You gave me.' משה only hinted this to them after forty years, and רבה learns from that timing that a student needs forty years to fully understand his teacher. רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי בנאה, explains a פסוק in ישעיהו: when ישראל are busy with תורה and גמילות חסדים, they control their יצר. תנא דבי אליהו adds that a person should carry תורה like an ox under a yoke and a donkey under a load. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's three-day ban on doing business with idolaters before their holidays. It asks why three days are needed, since people buy animals for a holiday only one day ahead. It answers that an animal bought for a sacrifice needs more preparation. Jews need thirty days because of their many blemish rules, but gentiles disqualify an animal only if it is missing a limb, so three days are enough. רבי אלעזר brings the source for that rule from the animals in נח's ark, and the גמרא begins to question that source. The challenge is completed on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof that ישראל are children of ingrates
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the פסוק about the מן that showed ישראל were כפויי טובה. It then brings a פסוק about אדם הראשון to show they were also 'children of' ingrates.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...with this light bread.' Children of ingrates, as it is written: 'The woman whom You gave to be with me, she gave me from the tree, and I ate.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof that began on the previous daf: משה called ישראל 'ingrates, children of ingrates.' Here it gives the source for the second half, 'children of ingrates,' from אדם הראשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people calling the מן 'light bread' shows they themselves were ungrateful. אדם הראשון blamed 'the woman You gave me' instead of being thankful for her. Since all people come from אדם, ישראל are 'children of' an ingrate.

keyTerms.meaning: Ingrates, people who deny the good done for them
'The light bread,' a scornful name for the מן

steps.confusionAlert: This step starts in the middle of a פסוק. The first half of the proof ('ingrates') was on the previous daf. This line only completes it and adds the 'children of ingrates' part.

phrases.english: with this light bread."
phrases.notes: This finishes a פסוק from the previous daf (במדבר 21:5), where the people were complaining about the מן.

phrases.english: Children of ingrates,
as it is written: "The woman whom You gave to be with me,

phrases.aramaic: הִיא נָתְנָה לִּי מִן הָעֵץ וָאֹכֵל״.
phrases.english: she gave me from the tree, and I ate."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun on the previous daf
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 3:12, where אדם הראשון blames the woman ה׳ gave him

steps.title: משה only hinted this after forty years
steps.stepSummary: Even משה רבינו did not hint to ישראל that they should have asked for a heart until forty years had passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even משה רבינו did not hint it to ישראל until after forty years, as it says: 'I led you in the wilderness forty years,' and it is written: 'But ה׳ did not give you a heart, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that משה himself waited forty years before hinting to ישראל what they should have asked for. It proves the timing from two neighboring פסוקים in דברים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק‎ 'ה׳ did not give you a heart to know' is the hint. The פסוק right next to it says 'I led you forty years,' so we know משה said it at the end of the forty years in the desert.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Etc.' The rest of the פסוק continues

phrases.english: Even Moshe our teacher
did not hint it to them, to Israel,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the point from the previous daf: they should have asked ה׳ to give them a heart to fear Him.

phrases.english: until after forty years,
as it is said: "And I led you in the wilderness forty years,"

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״וְלֹא נָתַן ה׳ לָכֶם לֵב וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: and it is written: "But ה׳ did not give you a heart, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 29:3. It goes on: 'to know, eyes to see, and ears to hear, until this day.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לֹא רְמָזָהּ לָהֶן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail about when משה rebuked ישראל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה hinted to ישראל about asking for a heart only after forty years in the desert

steps.title: A student needs forty years to fully understand his teacher
steps.stepSummary: רבה learns from משה's timing that a person does not truly grasp his teacher's mind until forty years have passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Learn from this that a person does not fully grasp his teacher's mind until forty years.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה draws a lesson from the previous step. Since משה waited forty years, it must take that long to truly understand one's רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה waited because ישראל could not yet understand him. Before that, they were not ready to hear such a hint. רבה turns this into a general rule about every student and teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: Fully grasps his mind (literally 'stands on his mind')

steps.whatToRemember: רבה: a person needs forty years to fully understand his teacher's way of thinking.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous principle about patience in learning. Real understanding of a רבי grows slowly over many years.

phrases.english: Rabbah said:
Learn from this
that a person does not fully grasp his teacher's mind
until forty years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general lesson from the forty-year delay
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A student does not fully understand his teacher until forty years have passed

steps.title: Happy are ישראל when they toil in תורה and kindness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי בנאה explains a פסוק in ישעיהו: when ישראל are busy with תורה and גמילות חסדים, they rule over their יצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי בנאה: What is meant by 'Happy are you who sow beside all waters, who send forth the feet of the ox and the donkey'? Happy are ישראל when they busy themselves with תורה and kindness. Their יצר is in their hands, and they are not in its hands, as it says: 'Happy are you who sow beside all waters.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רבי יוחנן quotes רבי בנאה, who explains a פסוק to mean that ישראל control their יצר when they learn תורה and do kindness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'מאי דכתיב' question is not a real challenge. It just opens the explanation of the פסוק. The key idea is control: תורה and kindness put the person in charge of his יצר instead of the other way around.

keyTerms.meaning: What is meant by what is written? (opens an explanation of a פסוק)
Handed over into their hands, under their control

steps.confusionAlert: 'מאי דכתיב' sounds like a question, but nobody is attacking anything. It simply opens a new explanation of a פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי בְּנָאָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Bana'ah:
What is meant by that which is written:
"Happy are you who sow beside all waters,
who send forth the feet of the ox and the donkey"?
Happy are Israel
when they busy themselves with Torah and with acts of kindness;
their inclination is handed over into their hands,
and they are not handed over into the hands of their inclination,
as it is said: "Happy are you who sow beside all waters."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי בְּנָאָה, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new אגדה teaching unrelated to the forty-years discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When ישראל engage in תורה and גמילות חסדים, they control their יצר and are not controlled by it

steps.title: Sowing means charity and water means תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from other פסוקים that 'sowing' refers to צדקה and 'water' refers to תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Sowing' means only צדקה, as it says: 'Sow for yourselves for charity, reap according to kindness.' 'Water' means only תורה, as it says: 'Ho, everyone who is thirsty, come to the water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי בנאה's reading. It shows from other פסוקים why 'sowing beside water' means kindness and תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word of the פסוק is linked to its meaning by another פסוק that uses the same word. In הושע, sowing goes with צדקה. In ישעיהו, water stands for תורה. That gives the two parts of the teaching: kindness and תורה.

phrases.english: And 'sowing' means nothing but charity,
as it is said: "Sow for yourselves for charity,
and reap according to kindness."
And 'water' means nothing but Torah,
as it is said: "Ho, everyone who is thirsty, come to the water."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading of the פסוק given in step 4
steps.raayaObject: That 'sowing beside water' means kindness and תורה

steps.title: Carry תורה like an ox under a yoke
steps.stepSummary: תנא דבי אליהו explains the second half of the פסוק: a person should bear the words of תורה like an ox bears a yoke and a donkey bears a load.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Who send forth the feet of the ox and the donkey': It was taught in the school of אליהו: A person should always place himself under the words of תורה like an ox under a yoke and like a donkey under a load.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second half of the same פסוק. תנא דבי אליהו uses the ox and donkey as a picture of how a person should carry תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ox pulls its yoke and a donkey carries its load steadily, without complaining. So too, a person should accept the effort and weight of learning תורה as his regular burden.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of אליהו

steps.whatToRemember: The whole פסוק is explained: 'sowing by water' means kindness and תורה, which give control over the יצר, and 'ox and donkey' means carrying תורה like a yoke and a load.

phrases.english: "Who send forth the feet of the ox and the donkey":
It was taught in the school of Eliyahu:
A person should always place himself
under the words of Torah
like an ox to the yoke
and like a donkey to the load.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְשַׁלְּחֵי רֶגֶל הַשּׁוֹר וְהַחֲמוֹר, תָּנָא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of the פסוק from step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should bear תורה like an ox bears a yoke and a donkey bears a load

steps.title: Do we really need three days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's three-day rule and asks whether such a long time is really needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said that for three days before their holidays it is forbidden to do business with idolaters. Do we really need that many days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and questions its three-day rule. This sets up the next step, where it brings a source to back up the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that three days seems like too long. If the idolater buys an animal for his holiday, why would he buy it three days early? The proof for this doubt comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: To do business (literally, to carry and to give)
And do we really need...? (opens a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים אָסוּר לָשֵׂאת וְלָתֵת עִמָּהֶם וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Three days it is forbidden to do business with them, etc.
phrases.notes: This is the line from our משנה about the days before the idolaters' holidays.

phrases.english: And do we really need all this much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the long introduction (which began on earlier dafim and ends in Steps 1-6), the גמרא now turns to explaining the משנה itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule of three days before the idolaters' holidays.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three days seems longer than people normally need to prepare an animal for a holiday.

steps.title: The משנה in חולין shows one day is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה showing that people buy animals for a יום טוב only on the day before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: On four times a year, someone who sells an animal must tell the buyer, 'I sold its mother to be slaughtered' or 'I sold its daughter to be slaughtered.' These are the eve of the last day of סוכות, the eve of the first day of פסח, the eve of שבועות, and the eve of ראש השנה. According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, also the eve of יום הכיפורים in the גליל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its question with a משנה from חולין. That משנה shows that people buy animals for a holiday just one day before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller must warn the buyer only on the day before the holiday, because that is when everyone buys meat to slaughter. So buying for a holiday happens one day ahead, not three. That makes the three-day rule look too long.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: On four occasions in the year,
one who sells an animal to his fellow must inform him:
"I sold its mother to be slaughtered,"
phrases.notes: He warns the buyer so he won't slaughter a mother and its young on the same day (ויקרא 22:28).

phrases.english: "I sold its daughter to be slaughtered."

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: עֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חַג,
phrases.english: And these are they: the eve of the last festival day of סוכות,

phrases.aramaic: עֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח,
phrases.english: the eve of the first festival day of פסח,
and the eve of שבועות, and the eve of ראש השנה,
and according to the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי —
also the eve of יום הכיפורים in the Galilee!
phrases.notes: In the גליל they had a big feast before יום הכיפורים, so meat was bought then too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the question in Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The doubt that three days are needed before a holiday.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in חולין: sellers warn buyers only on the day before a יום טוב, showing people buy one day ahead.

steps.title: Food takes one day, a קרבן takes three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: buying for eating needs one day, but buying for a sacrifice needs three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the animal is bought for eating, so one day is enough. Here, the animal is bought for a sacrifice, so three days are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by pointing out that the two cases are about different uses of the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In חולין the animal is meant for a holiday meal, which needs only one day to arrange. In our משנה the idolater buys it to sacrifice to his idol, which takes more preparation. That is why the משנה forbids business for three days.

phrases.english: There, where it is for eating, one day is enough.
Here, where it is for sacrifice, we need three days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 7-8 by separating the two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought all holiday animal purchases happen one day ahead, so three days is too much.
steps.terutzMaskana: Animals for eating are bought one day ahead; animals for sacrifice need three days.

steps.title: A קרבן should need even more than three days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: preparing for a קרבן seems to take thirty days, or at least two weeks.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for a sacrifice, are three days enough? But didn't we learn: We ask about the laws of פסח thirty days before פסח. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: two weeks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks its own answer. If a sacrifice needs more preparation, then three days is too little, not too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the קרבן פסח, people start learning its laws thirty days ahead, or two weeks according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. This shows that getting ready for a sacrifice takes much longer than three days. So why does our משנה stop at three days?
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the challenge has flipped. Before, three days looked too long. Now, for a sacrifice, three days looks too short.

phrases.english: And for sacrifice, are three days enough?
But didn't we learn: We ask about the laws of פסח
thirty days before פסח,

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: שְׁתֵּי שַׁבָּתוֹת.
phrases.english: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: two weeks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a sacrifice needs three days of preparation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Preparing for the קרבן פסח starts thirty days (or two weeks) ahead, so preparing for a sacrifice should need much more than three days.

steps.title: Jews need thirty days, gentiles need only three
steps.stepSummary: Jews must check for many small blemishes, so they need thirty days. Gentiles only disqualify an animal missing a limb, so three days are enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: We Jews, for whom disqualifying blemishes are common (even a spot on the eye's membrane disqualifies), need thirty days. They, who only have the rule of a missing limb, are fine with three days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 10. The long preparation time is a Jewish rule, and it does not apply to gentiles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a Jew, many tiny flaws can make an animal unfit for a קרבן, so a careful search takes a long time. A gentile's sacrifice is unfit only if a whole limb is missing, which is easy to see. That is why the משנה's three days are enough for gentiles.

keyTerms.meaning: Blemishes that make an animal unfit for a קרבן
The thin membrane of the eye; even a small mark there counts as a blemish

steps.confusionAlert: The thirty days is not a rule for gentiles. It is the Jewish preparation time, and the גמרא is explaining why gentiles need less.

phrases.english: We, for whom disqualifying blemishes are common,
even on the membrane of the eye,
phrases.notes: He means even a tiny mark on the eye makes the animal unfit for us.

phrases.english: we need thirty days;
they, who have only the rule of a missing limb,
three days are enough.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between cases: Jewish blemish rules versus gentile blemish rules
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every sacrifice needs thirty days of preparation, so three days seems too short.
steps.terutzMaskana: Thirty days applies only to Jews, who have many blemish rules. Gentiles only check for a missing limb, so three days are enough.

steps.title: Source that gentiles may not offer an animal missing a limb
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר learns from the animals brought into the ark that בני נח may not sacrifice an animal missing a limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אלעזר said: How do we know that an animal missing a limb is forbidden to בני נח? It says, 'And of every living thing of all flesh, two of every…'. The תורה is saying: bring an animal whose limbs are whole and alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the last step with a source. It shows that gentiles really do have the rule of מחוסר אבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'החי' ('living') is read as 'an animal whose limbs are all living,' meaning none are missing. These animals were later used by נח for sacrifices, so the rule applies to sacrifices of בני נח.

keyTerms.meaning: Descendants of נח, meaning all non-Jews

phrases.english: As Rabbi Elazar said:
From where do we know regarding an animal missing a limb
that it is forbidden to descendants of Noah?
As it is written: "And of every living thing of all flesh,
two of every… etc."
The Torah said: Bring an animal
whose limb-ends are alive.
phrases.notes: In other words, no limb is missing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the gentile rule mentioned in step 11
steps.raayaObject: The claim that gentiles have the rule of מחוסר אבר

steps.title: Isn't that verse needed to exclude a טריפה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether 'החי' is really needed to teach that a טריפה may not be offered, which would leave nothing for מחוסר אבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this phrase is needed to exclude a טריפה, teaching that it may not be offered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's source. It says the word 'החי' already has a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טריפה is an animal with a fatal injury, so it is not truly 'living.' If 'החי' teaches that a טריפה is unfit, it cannot also be used to teach about a missing limb.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal injury that will not survive

phrases.english: This is needed
to exclude a tereifa, that it is not fit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's use of 'החי' for מחוסר אבר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase is already used up to exclude a טריפה, so it cannot also teach about a missing limb.

steps.title: טריפה is learned from 'to keep seed alive'
steps.stepSummary: The טריפה rule comes from a different phrase, 'לחיות זרע,' so 'החי' is free to teach about a missing limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule of טריפה comes from 'to keep seed alive.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It moves the טריפה rule to a different phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animals in the ark had to be able to produce offspring. That excludes a טריפה, so 'החי' is left to teach the rule of a missing limb.

keyTerms.meaning: To keep seed alive, meaning able to have offspring

phrases.english: Tereifa is derived from "to keep seed alive."

steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning a different source to the other law
steps.terutzMaskana: טריפה comes from 'לחיות זרע,' so 'החי' teaches מחוסר אבר.

steps.title: This works only if a טריפה cannot give birth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the answer works only for the view that a טריפה cannot give birth. It is setting up a challenge from the opposite view.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who says a טריפה cannot give birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to question the last answer. It is setting up a challenge that is completed on the next amud (6a).
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לחיות זרע' excludes a טריפה only if a טריפה cannot have offspring. The word 'הניחא' signals that someone who holds a טריפה can give birth will have a problem with this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one view), hinting at a problem for another view
According to the one who says

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
a tereifa cannot give birth,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge to the answer of step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that טריפה is learned from 'לחיות זרע'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That source works only if a טריפה cannot give birth. The view that it can give birth is about to be raised.
